source_text: Quod enim et de alio libro meo, quem scripsi ad sanctae memoriae Marcellinum, velut mihi praescribens ponere voluisti, de Adam dictum, "quod tabificavit in se omnes de sua stirpe venturos"; … Sed verba quae ad rem maxime pertinent in eadem sententia mea, ego dicam, quia tu dicere noluisti; et statim cur nolueris apparebit. "Occulta - inquam - tabe carnalis concupiscentiae suae tabificavit in se omnes de sua stirpe venturos"
pass_a_gloss: For what also from another book of mine, which I wrote to Marcellinus of holy memory, as if raising an objection against me, you wished to place, said of Adam, 'that he wasted in himself all who would come from his stock'. But the words which most pertain to the matter in the same sentence of mine, I will say, because you did not want to say (them); and at once why you did not want will appear. 'By the hidden decay, I say, of his carnal concupiscence he wasted in himself all who would come from his stock.'

lemmas.gloss: entering a legal objection, ruling out in advance

pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “From another book of mine, which I wrote to Marcellinus of holy memory, you chose to set down, as though lodging an objection against me, what was said of Adam, ‘that he corrupted in himself all who were to come from his stock.’ … But the words in that same sentence of mine that matter most for the point, I will say, since you did not want to say them; and why you did not want to will at once be clear: ‘By the hidden decay of his fleshly desire,’ I said, ‘he corrupted in himself all who were to come from his stock.’”

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
